inline_comments.comment:
`line.split(/\s/g)` splits on any whitespace character (spaces, tabs, form-feeds, etc.). This produces **empty-string tokens** whenever there are leading/trailing spaces or consecutive spaces — e.g. `'Hello  World'` → `['Hello', '', 'World']`.

Because `createFormattedText` prepends a space before each word at index > 0, the empty token contributes an extra rendered space: `'Hello' + ' ' + '' + ' ' + 'World'` renders as `'Hello  World'` (two spaces). Tabs are also silently dropped rather than preserved or converted.

The original `createLabel` created a single tspan per line with `row.trim()`, preserving interior whitespace faithfully. To match that behaviour more closely, split only on a literal space character (or keep each line as a single word token):
```ts
line.trim().split(/ /g).map((word) => ({ content: word, type: 'normal' }))
```
Alternatively, represent each entire line as a single one-word `MarkdownLine` to avoid the word-splitting semantics entirely.

The `title-row` / `row` class is now applied to the parent `<text>` element, whereas the original `createLabel` applied it to each individual `<tspan>` element. Any CSS rule that targets `.title-row` or `.row` as an element-level class on a tspan (e.g. `.title-row { font-weight: bold }`) will no longer match. The inline comment acknowledges that no such CSS was found, but to be safe for downstream themes and custom CSS that consumers may have, the class should be applied to the tspan(s) inside `svgLabel` rather than the `text` element itself.

`getConfig()` is called twice in the same ternary expression:
```ts
const bodyFontSize = getConfig().fontSize
  ? getConfig().fontSize
  : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;
```
Call it once and cache the result:
```ts
const config = getConfig();
const bodyFontSize = config.fontSize
  ? config.fontSize
  : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;
```

The changeset is declared as `patch`, but the PR adds net-new user-visible features (KaTeX support and FontAwesome icon-pack rendering in label paths that previously lacked them). Per the project's changeset guidelines, adding features warrants a `minor` bump. The body already uses `fix:` as the conventional-commit prefix — if the intent is that these are only incidental fixes surfacing from the refactor rather than deliberate new feature gates, that reasoning should be stated explicitly in the changeset body.

The TODO comment `// TODO: the createText function returns a Promise, so I'm guessing it never runs?` points to a real bug: the markdown branch does not `await` `createText`, so `text` receives a `Promise` object instead of a DOM element, and the subsequent `text.getBBox()` will silently fail. This is a pre-existing issue that this PR surfaced but did not fix. Since the refactor explicitly touches this ternary, it is the right time to add the `await`:
```js
const text =
  node.labelType === 'markdown'
    ? await createText(label, node.labelText, { style: node.labelStyle, useHtmlLabels }, siteConfig)
    : await createLabel(label, node.labelText, node.labelStyle, undefined, true);
```
The same missing `await` exists in `dagre-wrapper/edges.js` for its markdown branch.

general_comments.comment: The new calling convention for `createLabel` (pass the parent element as the first argument, then call `getBBox()` / `getBoundingClientRect()` at the call site) requires callers to manually add an `if (useHtmlLabels)` block to resize the returned `foreignObject`. This boilerplate is now copy-pasted in eight separate places across `dagre-wrapper/edges.js`, `rendering-util/rendering-elements/edges.js`, and `nodes.js`. Consider extracting this resize step into a small helper, or having `createLabel` / `createText` return an object that includes the resolved bounding box, to remove the repeated pattern.

Multiple TODO comments remain in the submitted diff (`dagre-wrapper/clusters.js`, `dagre-wrapper/edges.js`, `rendering-util/rendering-elements/clusters.js`). At least one of them (`getClusterTitleWidth` missing `await`) is an actual correctness bug, not just a question. TODO comments should be resolved — either by fixing the issue in this PR or by converting them to tracked GitHub issues — rather than being merged as unanswered questions.
